Relative to neutral, the statement remains moderately hawkish: a 25 bp hike to 4.50–4.75%, explicit guidance for “ongoing increases,” and continued balance-sheet runoff. Operational settings (IORB at 4.65% and ON RRP at 4.55%) reinforce floor-system control of short rates, while QT and forward guidance shape the expected path and term premia.

Viewed through the Federal Reserve’s Financial Stability Report lens, vulnerabilities and tighter financial conditions—such as periodic strains in Treasury and agency MBS market liquidity, elevated interest rate volatility, and funding risks in parts of the nonbank sector—heighten the relevance of the Committee’s emphasis on policy lags, cumulative tightening, and close monitoring of financial developments. The acknowledgment that inflation has “eased somewhat” and the readiness to adjust policy if risks emerge further reflect this stability-aware posture.

Net: still a hawkish bias, but tempered by financial-stability considerations noted in the FSR. Adjusting slightly toward neutral from the prior assessment.
